addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.prompt:
I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this codebase — from the HTTP handler all the way down to the data/storage layer. 

Search very thoroughly for:
1. Routes/endpoints related to user avatar or profile image serving (look for patterns like "/avatar", "/photo", "/picture", "profile_image", "user image", etc.)
2. The handler function that serves the image
3. Any intermediate service/store/model layers between the handler and the actual data storage
4. How the image data is ultimately retrieved (from disk, database, object storage, etc.)

Look in routers, controllers, handlers, API definitions, services, stores, models. Check for patterns like "avatar", "profile_image", "user_image", "photo", "picture" in route definitions, handler files, service files, and store/repository files.

Be very thorough — search across multiple naming conventions and locations. Report every file path and function/method name involved in the chain.

content.text: I now have a thorough end-to-end trace. Here is the complete report. --- ## End-to-End Trace: Serving a User's Avatar Image This is the Memos project (github.com/usememos/memos), a Go application using the Echo HTTP framework with SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL backends. ### 1. Route Registration **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` (lines 81-82) The server's `NewServer` function creates a `FileServerService` and registers its routes on the Echo instance: ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125) `RegisterRoutes` mounts the avatar endpoint: ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` The browser hits: **`GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`** ### 2. How the URL is Constructed (API response side) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-42) Function `convertUserFromStore` builds the API User protobuf. If the stored `AvatarURL` is a base64 data URI, it replaces it with a file-server URL to avoid sending huge inline data: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL // external URL, serve as-is } } ``` `userpb.Name` has format `users/{username}`, so the final URL is `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. ### 3. The Handler Function: `serveUserAvatar` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 168-210) Function: `(*FileServerService).serveUserAvatar` Step-by-step logic: 1. **Authentication check (lines 172-181):** If the instance is private (`AllowAnonymous()` returns false, meaning no `InstanceURL` is configured), the handler requires a valid session. It calls `s.getCurrentUser()` which delegates to the `Authenticator`. 2. **Look up the target user (lines 183-194):** Extracts the `:identifier` path param (the username), calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)` which calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`. 3. **Parse the data URI (line 196):** Calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` which uses a regex to extract the MIME type and base64-decode the image bytes from the stored `data:image/...;base64,...` string. 4. **MIME type validation (lines 201-203):** Checks the image type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, HEIC, HEIF). 5. **Response (lines 205-209):** Sets security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP), sets `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, then sends the raw image bytes with `c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData)`. ### 4. Authentication Layer **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-712) ```go func (s *FileServerService) getCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, c *echo.Context) (*store.User, error) { authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get(echo.HeaderAuthorization) cookieHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Cookie") return s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader) } ``` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) `AuthenticateToUser` tries, in order: 1. Bearer token from `Authorization` header (Access Token V2 or Personal Access Token) 2. Refresh token from cookie (browser `` tag flow) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/extract.go` - `ExtractBearerToken` parses `Authorization: Bearer {token}` - `ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie` parses the refresh token from the `Cookie` header ### 5. User Lookup (Store Layer) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 715-717) ```go func (s *FileServerService) getUserByUsername(ctx context.Context, identifier string) (*store.User, error) { return s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}) } ``` **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) `(*Store).GetUser` first checks the in-memory cache (keyed by user ID). If the query is by username (no ID), it falls through to `ListUsers`, which calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)`. The result is cached by user ID. **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` (lines 13-30, 38-61) The `Store` struct holds a `userCache` of type `*cache.Cache` with a 10-minute TTL and max 1000 items. ### 6. Database Driver Layer The `Driver` interface is defined at `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` (line 48): ```go ListUsers(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) ([]*User, error) ``` Three implementations: - **SQLite:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) -- `ListUsers` queries `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE ...` and scans the `avatar_url` column into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189). - **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` -- same pattern, selects `avatar_url` column. - **MySQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` -- same pattern, selects `` `avatar_url` `` column. ### 7. Data Storage Model **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 29-45) The `User` struct has an `AvatarURL string` field (line 43). The avatar image data is stored **directly in the database** as a base64-encoded data URI in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table. The format is `data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...`. There is no separate file or object storage for avatars -- unlike attachments (which support local disk, S3, or database blob storage), avatars are always inline data URIs in the user row. ### 8. How Avatars Are Set (Upload Path) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` (lines 335-354) When a user updates their profile via the `UpdateUser` gRPC endpoint with `avatar_url` in the update mask, the handler validates the data URI MIME type against an allowlist and then stores it via `update.AvatarURL = &request.User.AvatarUrl`, which flows through `Store.UpdateUser` -> `driver.UpdateUser` -> SQL `UPDATE user SET avatar_url = ? WHERE id = ?`. **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` (line 64) SSO/OAuth2 login can also set an avatar URL from the identity provider's user info, in which case it may be an external URL rather than a data URI. When the stored value is an external URL (not parseable as `data:...;base64,...`), `convertUserFromStore` passes it through directly and `serveUserAvatar` is not used -- the browser fetches the external URL itself. ### 9. Proto Definition **File:** `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` (lines 228-229) ```proto string avatar_url = 6 [(google.api.field_behavior) = OPTIONAL]; ``` ### Summary of the Complete Call Chain ``` Browser GET /file/users/{username}/avatar | v Echo router -> FileServerService.serveUserAvatar() | [fileserver.go:168] | +-- (if private instance) FileServerService.getCurrentUser() | [fileserver.go:708] | -> Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser() | [authenticator.go:190] | -> resolveBearer() (Access Token V2 or PAT) | -> ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie() fallback | -> Store.GetUser() to resolve user from token | +-- FileServerService.getUserByUsername(identifier) | [fileserver.go:715] | -> Store.GetUser(&FindUser{Username: &identifier}) | [user.go:148] | -> check userCache (in-memory, 10min TTL) | -> Store.ListUsers() | [user.go:136] | -> driver.ListUsers() (Driver interface) | [driver.go:48] | -> sqlite/user.go:ListUsers (or postgres, mysql) | SQL: SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | -> rows.Scan(&user.AvatarURL) | -> populate cache | -> return *User (with AvatarURL field) | +-- FileServerService.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL) | [fileserver.go:737] | regex: ^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+) | -> base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(base64Data) | -> returns (mimeType string, imageBytes []byte) | +-- validate against avatarAllowedTypes | [fileserver.go:75-83] | +-- set security/cache headers, return c.Blob(200, mimeType, imageBytes) ``` ### Key Files in the Chain | Layer | File | Key Function/Type | |-------|------|-------------------| | Route registration | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` | `NewServer` (line 81) | | Route definition | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | `RegisterRoutes` (line 121) | | HTTP handler | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | `serveUserAvatar` (line 168) | | Data URI parsing | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | `parseDataURI` (line 737) | | Auth (shared) | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` | `AuthenticateToUser` (line 190) | | Token extraction | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/extract.go` | `ExtractBearerToken`, `ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie` | | URL construction (API) | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` | `convertUserFromStore` (line 16) | | Avatar upload validation | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` | `UpdateUser` handler (line 335) | | Store (business logic) | `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` | `GetUser` (line 148), `User` struct (line 29) | | Store (cache/wiring) | `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` | `Store` struct, `userCache` (line 29) | | Driver interface | `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` | `Driver.ListUsers` (line 48) | | SQLite driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` | `ListUsers` (line 88) | | PostgreSQL driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` | `ListUsers` | | MySQL driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` | `ListUsers` | | Profile config | `/bench/home/work/internal/profile/profile.go` | `AllowAnonymous` (line 46) | | Proto definition | `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` | `avatar_url` field (line 229) |
